claims.statement: Definition of the shifted lonely runner conjecture as pinned by the auditor from the sources: BCS arXiv 2603.24784 v4 Conj. 1.1(ii) (for distinct |v_i| and every s there is t with dist(s_i + v_i t, Z) >= 1/(n+1) for all i) and Def. 1.3 (gamma, gamma_sh); Zhang arXiv 2608.13599 v3 App. A and Question 8.5; Poliakova arXiv 2609.23952 v1 Sec. 1 (1/(n+1+E_n) = inf gamma). Consequence: gamma(v;s) < 1/(n+1) iff the OPEN arcs cover the circle (maximum attained); integer positive v and rational s lose no generality for counterexamples.

Prior results: the shifted conjecture is proved for n <= 4 (Alcantara-Criado-Santos; BCS Remark 1.2); it fails for n = 5..17 (BCS Prop. 5.14, as cited by the producer; BCS Table 2 gives exact gamma_sh(1..n) for n <= 15) and for every n >= 95 (Poliakova Thm 2, E_n >= 1); Zhang and Poliakova call 18 <= n <= 94 open (v3 of 18 Oct 2026; v1); BCS v4 (24 Oct 2026) states failure only for n = 5..17. Hence, with this paper, failure is known for n in 5..38 and n >= 95; n in 39..94 is open.

The producer's two checkers accept all 34 certificates n = 5..38 (re-checked from the stored JSON by verify_all.py): checker 1 (slr_exact.py, Python integers, greedy sweep of open integer intervals) and checker 2 (check_cover.c, __int128, every arc right endpoint strictly inside another arc). Different criteria and languages, SAME author: not independent in authorship.

The auditor's third checker (audit_check.py, written from scratch, standard library; exact Fractions) accepts all 34 certificates by two methods: A = exact interval subtraction of all open arcs from [0,1] (nothing left), B = exact gamma(v;s) over all pairwise-crossing and single-peak candidates, gamma < 1/(n+1). Re-run by us: 34/34 valid, both methods COVERED, gamma values identical to the auditor's table. Exact margins 1/gamma - (n+1) lie in [0.0961, 0.1098] for n = 18..38 (min n = 30, max n = 25), so E_n >= 0.096 (Poliakova's notation) and Gamma(n) < 1/(n+1) for these n; upper bounds only.

Controls. Producer: P1/P2 reproduce the published exact gamma 15/94 and 2/15; own shifts for [n], n = 5..17, certified; tangency at delta = gamma rejected; [n] with s = 0 never certified (n = 2..94); <= 14 speeds with s = 0 never certified (3005 instances); single-shift perturbation breaks 0/10 and 0/12 at the published deltas (reported, not hidden) and 4-10 per certificate on new ones. Auditor: [n], s = 0, n = 2..40, 0/39 covered; BCS gammas 15/94, 2/15, 9/67 reproduced; tangency at n = 5, 18, 29, 38 rejected at gamma and gamma - 1e-12, covered at gamma + 1e-12; invalid inputs flagged; delta/2 perturbations break 36/36 at n = 18 and 72/76 at n = 38; 0 disagreements between methods A and B; fuzz 400 x 4, 0 mismatches.

The 34 generated Lean files are about the certificates: for each n = 5..38 the typed literals v and s equal the certificate JSON (s_i = a_i/D), the cover statement is the template with only n substituted (delta = 1/(n+1)), v_injective and v_pos are present, the only import is Mathlib.Tactic and no sorry/admit/native_decide/axiom/unsafe/implemented_by occurs. A text check, not a proof; the kernel is the judge of cover.

HEADLINE. For every n in 18..38 there is an explicit exact certificate (distinct positive integers v_1..v_n, rationals s_i = a_i/D) that is a counterexample of size n to the shifted lonely runner conjecture (BCS Conj. 1.1(ii)): the open arcs of radius 1/(n+1) cover the circle, gamma(v;s) < 1/(n+1) exactly. Together with the literature the conjecture is known to fail for n in 5..38 and n >= 95; n in 39..94 stays open. Upper bounds only (Gamma(n) < 1/(n+1); E_n >= 0.096); nothing about the unshifted conjecture; NOT 'fails for all n >= 5'. Rests on: the Lean covering statements (Tier A pending a statement lock), the definition (L), three exact checkers (two same-author, one independent). Filed C because an assembly argument is capped at C.

Floating-point search and its absences: the search (cover_ls.py, cover_ls_fast.c) found certificates n <= 38 and none for n = 39..60 within 29.75 of the 30 core-hour cap (attempts: n=39 0/23, n=40 0/15, n=41..59 0/12 each, n=60 0/11; n = 61..94 never attempted). This supports no claim about n >= 39. The 333 raw scratch files logs/fast_tmp/*.txt are omitted from the bundle (not in the hash list of result.json).

Scoop check, a recorded search and not a proof of absence: alphaXiv (several recency windows up to published_after 2026-10-24) and web search on 2026-10-28 (producer) and 2026-10-31 (auditor) found no source settling any n in 18..94; residual risk: arXiv listings after the alphaXiv index, unpublished BCS/Criado computations, private communications. The cited authors have not been contacted.

NOT run: anse/formal/lean_runner.py and a statement lock on the 32 files other than n = 18 and n = 38 (the auditor ran lean_pinned.py only); no human audit; pytest tests/ and the repository guards were not run for this paper. Recorded so the absences are explicit.
